name: Laurel Ridge Country Club
title: Laurel Ridge Wedding DJ & Host | Dan's Events
description: A guide to weddings at Laurel Ridge Country Club in Waynesville, NC: the Grand Lodge, Rustic Pavilion and Arbor, with notes on sound and lighting.
h1: Planning sound, hosting and lighting at Laurel Ridge Country Club
lede: Laurel Ridge is a golf club in Waynesville, about 30 minutes west of Asheville, with a stone-and-beam Grand Lodge, a covered Rustic Pavilion and an Arbor that looks out over the course. Here is how the spaces work and what I would ask.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: 49 Cupp Lane, Waynesville, NC 28786, which the venue describes as 30 minutes west of Asheville.

facts.label: Grand Lodge
facts.value: Seated capacity 175, cocktail style 250. Stonework, rustic beams, cathedral ceilings and walls of windows overlooking the golf course.

facts.label: Rustic Pavilion
facts.value: Seated capacity 200, cocktail style 250. A covered outdoor venue with a full bar, deck and stone fireplace hearth, with heating elements and clear drop-down sides.

facts.label: The Arbor
facts.value: Ceremony only, seated capacity 250. Natural laurel branches and poplar posts, adjacent to the Rustic Pavilion.

facts.label: Event time
facts.value: One hour of rehearsal and five hours of event time are included for every wedding. The Bridal Suite opens at 9 a.m.

sections.h2: Three spaces on the golf course
p: The Grand Lodge is the indoor room, with stonework, rustic beams, cathedral ceilings and walls of windows toward the course. The Rustic Pavilion is a covered outdoor space with a deck, a full bar and a stone fireplace hearth, plus heating elements and clear drop-down sides for cool evenings. The Arbor is for ceremonies only, built from natural laurel branches and poplar posts.

The Arbor sits next to the Pavilion, so a ceremony and a reception can happen a few steps apart. Smaller rooms in the Lodge, the Mountain Vista Room and the Cedar Room, are used for rehearsal dinners and similar events.

sections.h2: Sound and hosting in each room
p: The Pavilion and the Lodge call for different plans. In the Lodge, cathedral ceilings and glass make a large reflective room, so I aim speakers into the crowd and keep the level controlled. In the Pavilion, the sides can be down for heat or up for air, so I check the sound both ways at the sound check.

The five-hour event time shapes the host's job. I plan the entrance, toasts, dinner, first dance and open floor to fit inside it, and the venue says extra event hours can be added when pre-arranged. Laurel Ridge does not publish a music cutoff or sound rules in the materials I found, so I ask the events team.

Stone, beams and windows make the Lodge a good canvas for warm white light. I would wash the beams, light faces and leave the window wall alone, so guests see the course at dusk. In the Pavilion, I would keep fixtures low and out of the way of the fireplace and the drop-down sides.

Low fog needs its own dedicated 30 amp circuit because it draws up to 3,000 watts for about five minutes at warm-up. Lights and sound run on ordinary 20 amp circuits. The venue does not publish its power layout or a rule on fog, cold sparks or open flame in the guide I read, so I would ask the events team and get approval in writing.

Lodging on site includes the Inn on the Green with four guest rooms, a one-bedroom First Tee Condo, the two-bedroom Condo on the Green and The Hideaway. Wedding packages include an in-house wedding planner, and food and beverage are separate from the venue fee.

The Bridal Suite is included with the Lodge and Pavilion packages from 9 a.m., and the Tee-Box Tavern is set aside for groomsmen. The guide does not publish a rain plan. The Pavilion has a roof, so ask whether your ceremony would move there from the Arbor.

faq.q: Is Laurel Ridge close to Asheville?
faq.a: The venue says it is conveniently located 30 minutes west of Asheville, in Waynesville. Check your own route and timing for the day.

faq.q: Can I bring my own DJ and host?
faq.a: The venue's wedding page lists bands and DJs among its vendor recommendations. I would ask the events team to confirm in writing that an outside DJ and host can work with your package.

faq.q: How long does the event run?
faq.a: Every wedding gets one hour of rehearsal and five hours of event time. Extra hours can be added if pre-arranged.

faq.q: Can we use cold sparks or fog?
faq.a: The materials I read do not publish a rule on either. I ask for written approval for your room and date.
